tasks.short: Pull labour market figures, CAO wage tables, agency rates and sector reports into one place for HR analysis.

today.trigger: A recurring monthly update, or an HR Director or HRBP question such as 'are we paying below the market in Venlo?'
steps: Download CBS StatLine and UWV tables on vacancies, unemployment and wages for the logistics sector and the three regions
Read sector reports (TLN, staffing agency market updates) and copy key numbers into Excel
Collect flex worker rates and volumes from the three agency portals
Clean, label and date the figures, then load them into the Power BI dataset next to the AFAS extract
drudgery: Re-downloading the same tables each month
Retyping numbers from PDFs
Matching region and sector codes across sources
today.time_sinks: Finding the latest version of each source and copying figures out of PDFs and portals by hand.

lenses.faster: Scheduled API pulls from CBS StatLine and agency exports replace manual downloads; an LLM extracts figures from PDF reports into a fixed table with page references.
lenses.autonomous: A monthly job refreshes the external tables and flags new releases or breaks in series before the dashboards refresh.
lenses.ambitious: A full external benchmark per site and job family (warehouse operator, driver, planner) refreshed monthly instead of an ad hoc lookup twice a year.
lenses.joy: No more copying numbers from PDFs; the analyst spends the time judging which sources are trustworthy.
lenses.options: Pull several benchmark sources side by side so HR sees a range rather than one number.
lenses.altitude: The analyst curates the source list and extraction rules and checks the quarterly source audit instead of collecting data.
reach: Compensation and Benefits Specialist market pay benchmarking
Recruiter labour market briefs for hard-to-fill roles
FP&A Analyst flex labour cost assumptions

tasks.human_edge: Judging which sources are reliable, comparable and allowed to be used, and spotting when a number does not make sense for Noordhaven's sites.
tasks.pattern_why: Most sources are structured and can be pulled by scheduled code; the PDF reports need an LLM to turn text into a checkable table inside that pipeline.

in_practice.trigger: Monthly schedule, plus a new-publication check on each registered source
steps: Scheduled script pulls CBS StatLine and UWV tables via API and loads agency portal exports
LLM extracts named figures from new PDF reports into a fixed schema with source page and date
Validation rules check ranges and series breaks against last month
Analyst reviews flagged items and approves the refresh
in_practice.human_gate: Analyst approves flagged values and any new source before it feeds dashboards.
data_needed: Source register with URLs and licence terms
in_practice.logs_to: Source log on SharePoint with retrieval date, source, extracted values and reviewer

evidence.claim: CBS StatLine offers open data through an OData API.
Job posting data for the Dutch market is sold as a structured feed.
LLMs extract tabular figures from PDF reports accurately enough when outputs are validated against ranges.

risks: Licence terms of purchased reports may forbid automated extraction
Silent errors in extracted numbers if validation is weak
Agency portal formats change without notice
research_questions: Which of the current sources have an API or stable export, and which are PDF only?
How many extraction errors does an LLM make on the last 12 months of sector reports compared with the manual copy?
Do the agency contracts allow exporting rate and volume data for analysis?

tasks.short: Tell HR and managers what changed in dashboards, reports and definitions, and how to use them.

today.trigger: A dashboard release, a changed metric definition, or repeated questions from managers
steps: Write a short note on what changed in the Power BI report or metric
Post it in the HR Teams channel and email site managers
Update the how-to page on SharePoint
Answer follow-up questions one by one in Teams and mail
drudgery: Rewriting the same explanation for different audiences
Answering the same 'why did the number change' question repeatedly
today.time_sinks: Follow-up questions after each change, often because managers did not read the note.

lenses.faster: Release notes are drafted from the change log and definition diff, in Dutch and English, for HR and for site managers.
lenses.autonomous: Publishing a report version triggers a draft note and an update to the metric glossary page.
lenses.ambitious: Every dashboard gets a living glossary and a Teams Q&A assistant answering 'what does this number mean' from the approved definitions.
lenses.joy: Fewer repeat questions; the analyst explains only the interesting changes.
lenses.options: Short Teams post, longer manager briefing and a one-line in-report banner from the same source.
lenses.altitude: The analyst maintains the definitions and change log that drive all communication.
reach: HR Business Partner manager briefings on HR metrics
L&D Specialist short training on dashboard use
Controller notes on shared HR-finance figures

tasks.human_edge: Knowing which change matters to whom and how a site manager will read a drop in a number.
tasks.pattern_why: Structured input (change log, definition diff) becomes a checkable draft text inside a fixed release workflow.

in_practice.trigger: New version of a Power BI report or a definition change merged into the metric glossary
steps: Collect change log entries and definition diffs for the release
LLM drafts release notes per audience and updates the glossary page
Analyst reviews and approves
Power Automate posts to the Teams channel and SharePoint page
in_practice.human_gate: Analyst approves each note before it is posted.
in_practice.logs_to: SharePoint release notes page with version history

evidence.claim: Power Automate can post to Teams channels on a trigger.
Microsoft 365 Copilot drafts summaries and posts from documents in Teams and Outlook.
A glossary-based Q&A assistant reduces repeat questions on metric meaning.

risks: A wrong explanation spreads quickly to managers
Q&A assistant answering beyond approved definitions
research_questions: How many repeat questions per month follow a dashboard release today?
Is there a clean change log to draft from, or does one need to be introduced first?
Do site managers read Teams posts, or would an in-report banner work better?

tasks.short: Write the spec for a new HR report or dashboard: purpose, metrics, filters, data sources, access rules.

today.trigger: A request from the HR Director, an HRBP or Finance for a new report or a change
steps: Hold an intake meeting with the requester
Write the spec in Word: questions, metrics, definitions, sources, refresh, access
Check field availability in the AFAS extract and Recruitee
Agree access and privacy rules, sometimes with the privacy officer
Get sign-off and file it on SharePoint
drudgery: Turning meeting notes into a structured document
Looking up field names and existing definitions
Documenting the existing data model after the fact
today.time_sinks: Back-and-forth with requesters on vague requirements and documenting existing reports nobody specified.

lenses.faster: The intake meeting transcript becomes a spec draft in the standard template, with fields matched to the existing data dictionary.
lenses.autonomous: Technical documentation of the Power BI model (tables, measures, lineage) is regenerated on each publish.
lenses.ambitious: Every HR report has a current spec and data dictionary, including the old ones nobody wrote down.
lenses.joy: No writing up of meeting notes; the analyst spends the time on what the requester actually needs.
lenses.options: Draft two or three report designs (one KPI page, a drill-down, a monthly PDF) for the requester to choose from.
lenses.altitude: The analyst owns the spec template and data dictionary that make new requests quick to specify.
reach: HR Administrator data entry rules
Controller definitions for shared headcount and FTE figures
Privacy officer DPIA input for HR reports

tasks.human_edge: Drawing out what the requester really wants and deciding what is sensible, including privacy and works council sensitivities.
tasks.pattern_why: Requirements come from conversation and judgement; AI drafts and looks up, the analyst leads and signs off.

in_practice.trigger: A new report request logged in the HR request list
steps: Record and transcribe the intake meeting in Teams
AI drafts the spec in the template and maps metrics to the data dictionary
AI lists missing fields and open questions
Analyst edits, resolves questions with the requester and gets sign-off
in_practice.human_gate: Analyst and requester sign off the spec; privacy check for personal data.
in_practice.logs_to: SharePoint spec library with version history

evidence.claim: Teams meeting transcripts can be summarised into structured notes by Copilot.
Power BI model metadata (tables, measures) can be exported for documentation.
Power BI shows lineage from source to report.

risks: Recording intake meetings needs consent
Spec looks complete but misses the real question
Data dictionary drift if not maintained
research_questions: How many current HR reports have no spec today?
Does a drafted spec cut the number of revision rounds with requesters?
Is the works council agreement on recording Teams meetings in place?

tasks.short: Turn HR trend data into a recommendation, e.g. why 90-day retention dropped in Tilburg and what to do.

today.trigger: Quarterly HR review, OR meeting preparation, or a question from the HR Director
steps: Pull trends from Power BI on hires, 90-day retention, verzuim and flex use
Slice by site, shift, job family and source (agency vs direct)
Look for causes in exit reasons, onboarding completion and Studytube certificates
Write a short memo or slides with findings and options
Discuss with HR Director and HRBPs
drudgery: Running the same slices every quarter
Building charts and slides
Re-explaining definitions in each memo
today.time_sinks: Exploring many slices to find the few that matter, then formatting slides.

lenses.faster: AI runs the standard slices, flags significant changes and drafts the memo with charts; the analyst checks and sharpens.
lenses.autonomous: A monthly trend scan flags unusual moves in retention, verzuim or time to hire per site.
lenses.ambitious: Each value stream (hire to productive, absence to return) gets a monthly driver analysis, not just a quarterly look.
lenses.joy: Less slide building, more time testing explanations with HRBPs and site managers.
lenses.options: Three to five candidate explanations and matching actions, each with the evidence for and against.
lenses.altitude: The analyst designs the trend scan and the standard driver model and reviews its output.
reach: HR Business Partner site-level people reviews
FP&A Analyst workforce cost scenarios
Recruiter source-of-hire quality analysis

tasks.human_edge: Knowing the context behind the numbers (a site reorganisation, a new agency, a hot summer) and making a recommendation the HR Director will stand behind.
tasks.pattern_why: The recommendation carries judgement and accountability; AI does the slicing and drafting.

in_practice.trigger: Monthly trend scan result or a quarterly review date
steps: Scheduled analysis runs standard slices and tests for significant change
AI drafts findings, candidate causes and charts
Analyst checks the numbers, adds context from HRBPs
Analyst writes the recommendation and presents it
in_practice.human_gate: Analyst owns the conclusions; HR Director decides on action.
in_practice.logs_to: Analysis folder on SharePoint with query, data snapshot and memo

evidence.claim: Power BI Copilot generates narrative summaries of report pages.
Power BI key influencers visual identifies drivers of an outcome.
LLM-drafted analytical memos still need human checking for false causal claims.

risks: Plausible but wrong causal stories
Small groups making individuals identifiable (AVG)
Over-reliance on automated flags
research_questions: Which of last year's recommendations would a trend scan have flagged earlier?
How often do AI-drafted causes survive a check with HRBPs?
What minimum group size is needed per slice to avoid identifying people?

tasks.short: Test that HR reports and dashboards show the right numbers and answer what was asked.

today.trigger: A new dashboard release, a change in AFAS setup, or a complaint about a wrong number
steps: Reconcile headcount and FTE in Power BI with AFAS and payroll
Spot-check individual records for edge cases (rehires, flex to permanent, long-term sick)
Check filters and row-level security per site and role
Walk through the report with the requester against the spec
drudgery: Manual reconciliations in Excel
Re-testing everything after each AFAS change
Checking access as each user role
today.time_sinks: Tracing why two systems disagree, often after the nightly extract changed.

lenses.faster: Reconciliation and data tests run as code after each nightly refresh instead of by hand before releases.
lenses.autonomous: Failed tests block the dashboard refresh notice and post the difference to the analyst in Teams.
lenses.ambitious: Every HR metric has automated tests, including row-level security per site, so managers trust the numbers.
lenses.joy: No Excel reconciliations; the analyst investigates only real differences.
lenses.options: AI proposes test cases from the spec and from known edge cases.
lenses.altitude: The analyst designs the test suite and acceptance criteria rather than running checks.
reach: Controller reconciliation of headcount cost with the ledger
Payroll Specialist checks of payroll-relevant HR changes
HR Administrator data quality fixes

tasks.human_edge: Deciding what 'right' means when systems disagree and accepting a report as fit for the requester.
tasks.pattern_why: Reconciliation and test rules can be written down and checked on structured data without a model at runtime.

in_practice.trigger: Nightly AFAS extract refresh and each report publish
steps: Run reconciliation tests (headcount, FTE, hires, leavers) against AFAS totals
Run edge-case and row-level security tests
Post failures with record-level differences to Teams
Analyst investigates and signs off releases
in_practice.human_gate: Analyst handles failures and accepts new reports with the requester.
in_practice.logs_to: Test results table with run date, test, result and fix note

evidence.claim: Data test frameworks run assertions on tables after each load.
AFAS Profit exposes data through GetConnectors for automated extraction.
Row-level security roles can be tested with 'view as role' in Power BI.

risks: Tests cover only known failure modes
Alert fatigue if thresholds are too tight
Test data contains personal data and needs access control
research_questions: How many wrong-number incidents last year would automated reconciliation have caught?
Can AFAS control totals be pulled automatically each night?
What is the effort to write tests for the top 20 HR metrics?

tasks.short: Track how competing employers and agencies recruit and pay warehouse staff and drivers in our regions.

today.trigger: Hiring trouble at a site, peak season planning, or CAO negotiation preparation
steps: Search job sites for competing vacancies in Rotterdam, Tilburg and Venlo
Note wages, shift allowances, bonuses and contract terms in Excel
Compare with Noordhaven's CAO scales and agency rates
Write a short summary for the HR Director and recruiters
drudgery: Reading dozens of vacancies by hand
Normalising hourly, monthly and allowance figures
today.time_sinks: Manual collection of vacancy details and making them comparable.

lenses.faster: A purchased job posting feed plus an LLM that extracts pay, allowances and terms into a fixed table replaces manual reading.
lenses.autonomous: A monthly competitor pay and offer overview per region is produced without a request.
lenses.ambitious: Continuous view of the regional labour market, linked to Noordhaven's own offer acceptance and time to hire.
lenses.joy: No copying vacancy texts; the analyst works on what the comparison means.
lenses.options: Scenarios: match market pay, add a shift bonus, or shift the agency mix, each with cost and expected effect.
lenses.altitude: The analyst defines the comparison basis and checks the monthly overview.
reach: Compensation and Benefits Specialist pay positioning
Recruiter vacancy text and offer design
HR Director CAO negotiation preparation

tasks.human_edge: Reading what competitor moves mean for Noordhaven and how far the company can respond within the CAO.
tasks.pattern_why: Several sources, messy texts and exceptions; a person checks before the overview informs pay or recruiting decisions.

in_practice.trigger: Monthly schedule or a request ahead of peak season
steps: Agent pulls postings for target roles and regions from a licensed feed
LLM extracts wage, allowances, hours and contract type into a table
Agent compares with CAO scales and agency rates and drafts an overview
Analyst reviews outliers and approves before sharing
in_practice.human_gate: Analyst approves the overview before it goes to HR Director and recruiters.
data_needed: Own offer acceptance data from Recruitee
in_practice.logs_to: Market overview folder on SharePoint with source snapshots

evidence.claim: Aggregated Dutch job posting data with salary fields is available commercially.
Job posting trend data is published for the Netherlands.
LLMs reliably extract pay and allowance terms from Dutch vacancy texts.

risks: Scraping job sites may break terms of use
Posted pay differs from paid pay
Sharing competitor pay data could raise competition law concerns if coordinated with other employers
research_questions: What does a licensed posting feed cost for three regions and five job families?
How well does posted pay match what candidates report in Recruitee offer declines?
Does the overview change decisions on offers or agency mix?

tasks.short: Produce required HR reports: verzuim figures, social annual report for the OR, CBS surveys, pay gap figures.

today.trigger: Fixed deadlines: monthly verzuim report, OR meeting, annual report, CBS survey, pay transparency reporting
steps: Pull data from AFAS and Power BI
Calculate figures per required definition (CBS verzuim, FTE, gender pay gap)
Fill templates in Excel and Word
Check with Payroll and Controller
Send to HR Director, OR or authority
drudgery: Recalculating the same figures in each template
Copying tables into Word
Re-checking definitions each year
today.time_sinks: Matching external definitions and reconciling with payroll before submission.

lenses.faster: Required figures are calculated by fixed, tested queries and filled into templates; an LLM drafts the narrative text.
lenses.autonomous: Recurring reports generate on schedule and land in the analyst's queue for review.
lenses.ambitious: Pay gap analysis per job family and site done properly ahead of the EU Pay Transparency Directive, not a single headline number.
lenses.joy: No copying tables into Word; time goes to explaining the figures to the OR.
lenses.options: Draft both a short OR version and a detailed management version from one dataset.
lenses.altitude: The analyst owns the definitions and the reporting pipeline and checks each submission.
reach: HR Administrator monthly verzuim reporting
Controller headcount and personnel cost notes in the annual report
Compensation and Benefits Specialist pay equity reporting

tasks.human_edge: Accountability for figures sent to the works council and authorities, and explaining sensitive outcomes such as a pay gap.
tasks.pattern_why: Definitions are fixed and data is structured; code produces checkable figures, with an LLM only for draft narrative.

steps: Scheduled queries calculate required figures from the AFAS extract
Reconciliation checks against payroll totals
Templates filled automatically; LLM drafts commentary
Analyst reviews, adjusts and sends
in_practice.human_gate: Analyst signs off; HR Director approves external and OR submissions.
in_practice.logs_to: Reporting archive on SharePoint with figures, queries and sign-off

evidence.claim: Power BI paginated reports produce fixed-format reports on a schedule.
Copilot in Word drafts text from provided data and documents.
The EU Pay Transparency Directive requires gender pay gap reporting by employers above size thresholds.

risks: Definition errors repeat silently every period
Small groups in OR reports identifying individuals (AVG)
Narrative overstating causes of a pay gap
research_questions: Which required reports have stable definitions that can be coded now?
When will the Dutch pay transparency law apply to Noordhaven and with what job categorisation?
How much time does reconciliation with payroll take per report today?

tasks.short: Keep our library of report templates, DAX measures, SQL snippets and metric definitions tidy and current.

today.trigger: New report built, definition changed, or someone cannot find the right template
steps: Save new templates and queries to SharePoint
Update the metric definition list
Remove or mark outdated versions
Tell colleagues where to find things
drudgery: Tagging and filing documents
Finding duplicates and stale versions
Keeping definitions in sync with the Power BI model
today.time_sinks: Duplicates and outdated files that nobody dares to delete.

lenses.faster: An LLM tags new items, detects near-duplicates and compares definitions with the live Power BI measures.
lenses.autonomous: A monthly sweep lists stale, duplicate or conflicting items for the analyst to approve archiving.
lenses.ambitious: A single searchable catalogue of HR metrics, measures and templates that HRBPs and Finance actually use.
lenses.joy: No filing; the analyst decides which definition wins.
lenses.options: AI proposes merges of overlapping templates with the differences shown.
lenses.altitude: The analyst sets the catalogue structure and rules and approves changes.
reach: L&D Specialist template library for course reports
Controller shared definition list for HR-finance figures
HR Administrator document templates on SharePoint

tasks.human_edge: Deciding which definition is the official one and agreeing it with Finance and HR.
tasks.pattern_why: Unstructured documents become tagged, compared catalogue entries inside a fixed maintenance workflow.

in_practice.trigger: New file in the library and a monthly sweep
steps: LLM classifies and tags new items against the catalogue scheme
Script compares glossary definitions with Power BI measures
Sweep lists duplicates, stale and conflicting items
Analyst approves archiving and definition fixes
in_practice.human_gate: Analyst approves each archive or definition change.
in_practice.logs_to: SharePoint version history and a catalogue change log

evidence.claim: SharePoint Premium can auto-classify and tag documents.
Power BI measure definitions can be exported for comparison with a glossary.
LLMs detect near-duplicate templates reliably enough for review lists.

risks: Wrong archiving removes a template still in use
Catalogue not adopted by colleagues
research_questions: How many duplicate or stale items are in the library now?
Do HRBPs and Finance search the catalogue or ask the analyst?
Is SharePoint Premium licensed, or is a simple script enough?

role.altitude: From building reports and pulling data to owning Noordhaven's HR data product: definitions, pipelines, tests and the trend scans that run themselves, with the analyst reviewing and advising.
reach: Compensation and Benefits Specialist market pay benchmarking and pay gap analysis
HR Administrator recurring verzuim and headcount reporting
Recruiter labour market briefs and source-of-hire analysis
Controller and FP&A Analyst workforce cost and flex labour scenarios
HR Business Partner site-level people reviews
role.ceiling_note: About 40% of the analyst's time across these tasks could be freed. The limits are data quality in AFAS and the agency portals, works council consent for new uses of personnel data (WOR art. 27), AVG limits on small groups and profiling, and EU AI Act high-risk rules if analytics start informing decisions about individual workers.
skills_to_grow: Data pipeline and test engineering (SQL, Python, dbt-style tests)
Metric governance and definition ownership with Finance
Privacy by design and DPIA input under AVG
Evaluating LLM outputs and setting review gates
Telling a clear story to the OR and the HR Director
role.ambitious_version: A monthly people intelligence service across the four value streams that links hiring, onboarding, certificates, verzuim and flex use to the North Star of 90-day productive hires, with automated tests and external benchmarks, so HR can act per site within weeks instead of once a year.
